hints.title: Distinct Drivers Base Table
hints.text: Extract the distinct driver_id list from Rides to form the base population.

hints.title: Left Join on Passenger Occurrences
hints.text: Left join distinct drivers with Rides matching driver_id to passenger_id.

hints.title: Count Aggregation
hints.text: Group by driver_id and count matching ride_id values (which counts 0 when null).

hints.title: Left Join Aggregation Query
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT
    d.driver_id,
    COUNT(r.ride_id) AS cnt
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT driver_id FROM Rides) d
LEFT JOIN Rides r
    ON d.driver_id = r.passenger_id
GROUP BY d.driver_id;
```

complexity.notes: Distinct driver scan and left join with group by aggregation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: An inner join drops drivers who were never passengers, omitting them from the result instead of showing 0.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Temporary grouping buffer stores distinct driver aggregates.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate utilizes LEFT JOIN and COUNT(r.ride_id) to correctly yield 0 for non-passenger drivers.

solutions.approach: Pandas Left Merge and Groupby Count
solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def count_driver_as_passenger(rides: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    drivers = pd.DataFrame({'driver_id': rides['driver_id'].unique()})
    passenger_counts = rides['passenger_id'].value_counts().reset_index()
    passenger_counts.columns = ['driver_id', 'cnt']
    merged = drivers.merge(passenger_counts, on='driver_id', how='left')
    merged['cnt'] = merged['cnt'].fillna(0).astype(int)
    return merged
